The USA is due for a new recession this year or next. The furious drive towards the capitalistic climate we have now has basically ensured that this will happen. And it happens almost like clockwork, although the hands on the clock are fuzzy. This has been caused by the out of control spiral of the drive for profit. When a business pushes employee wages down, they have less money to spend, they borrow to spend and when the economy can not longer handle the weight of non existing money, it collapses and start again.

So how can a business or individual who wants to invest ensure they are not caught up in this ridiculous cycle? The answer, not just in this case but in all questions like this, is diversity.

For those who do not wish to own a business, I will list the 3 that I currently like to tell people about. There is a cash market (debt and currency). There is a real estate market. There is a stock market.

**Cash**

Cash is by far the most dangerous investment you can make. Particularly for the USA and specially this year. The investments that cover this are things like loans and cash interest. There are places that allow you to loan out your money to people who need it and pretty much every bank in existence offer interest for holding money. Be in in a cash holding account or a term deposit. Cash is effected by inflation and the national bank interest rate. Many European countries currently have such a bad interest rate that they are penalising people for keeping money, so term deposits and long term investments are all that is available to them.

Cash is also super dangerous as most countries have a fiat currency. That is, money that is printed and not actually worth anything. There are a few countries that have fallen into this trap in the news recently.

Cash is still important and every business should have cash investments to some degree, even if it is just spare money they are not using until an emergency. It is liquid, meaning you can get at it instantly. It however, has the lowest rate of return.

**Real estate** Yes, it is expensive. In Australia it is hard as most people can not afford outside their own home. In the USA you are able to tax against your own personal home, so it is not so bad. In Australia you are able to use your retirement funds (super) to buy property. Most people do not know this. I am not sure if you can use a 401K in america to do this. I don't believe so. That being said, a joint venture between several close friends or family, combining money to buy property is at times something to consider. This also doesn't just apply to houses and commercial buildings. You can buy car parks in cities, or moors in marinas. There are a variety of space related things you can own and rent out. If you are able to get something, it is always an investment.

**Stock Market** Most people know how this works. I wont go into the details of how you should trade, but if you know of a good company that is going places, buying this stock is a good investment.

---

The reason diversity saves you from economic collapse is quite simple. While a recession drives everything down, it does not kill everything. In the event that cash fails or the interest rate drops to 0, you have real estate and shares to support you. If the market crashes because the entire Chinese economy drowned in the sea, you have cash and real estate. If the real estate market is destroyed due to debt or over valuation, you still have cash and shares.

If you as a person or business, put all of your money into one investment and it loses, you have not practiced sustainability.
Investment diversity. How to gain some control in the mess of the economy cycle.
